title: The Electronic Signatures Market is one of the Smallest Industries for Investment | DOCU Stock News
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc revisits DocuSign after a run from about $40 to over $82 per share, up more than 21% year to date in 2026, and asks whether it is still a buying opportunity after doubling. Agentic AI has not killed the business as some feared: DocuSign has connected into Slack, Google Gemini and other platforms to stay the signature of choice. His long-held view is that the electronic-signature market is too small — under $100 billion of annual spend — for bigger rivals to bother stealing DocuSign's dominant position, and that paper signing makes sense for only 5-10% of cases, so e-signatures should keep growing toward about 90% of all signings. Wall Street expects 14.7% medium-to-long-term EPS growth; he expects a lower 11-12%. Revenue per employee has nearly doubled since 2019, from about $250,000 to $463,000 over the trailing twelve months, which he reads as AI-driven productivity. Valuation has followed the price: forward PE is now 15.9, nearly double the sub-10x level earlier in 2026 when he flagged an excellent buying opportunity, giving a PEG of about one against 14.7% growth. His updated DCF value is $101 versus an $83 market price. Call: DOCU — BUY (reiterated, first tracked call; ranked a buying opportunity all year, last updated 26 June 2026) — still undervalued, but with downgraded conviction as the price approaches fair value.
